crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice covers the use of data and models to tailor portfolio recommendations to an individual's goals, time horizon, tax position, liquidity needs, and tolerance for loss.

children.name: Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance
children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance covers methods that go past expected return and variance as the only summary of a portfolio.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in portfolio construction covers the deliberate use of instruments and overlays to limit losses from rare, severe market moves, such as crashes, volatility spikes, or correlation breakdowns.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios are the environmental, social and governance characteristics of holdings that investors use alongside financial measures.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers the valuation of holdings that do not trade on a public market, such as private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, and stakes in private companies.

sections.body: Portfolio construction is the work of choosing and weighting assets so that a pool of capital meets a set of goals, constraints and risk tolerances. Artificial intelligence is now used in this field for return forecasting, risk estimation, factor discovery, trade execution and the automation of rebalancing. Machine learning models read market data, alternative data and text, then feed optimisers that propose allocations. In personalised advice, AI systems try to translate an individual's circumstances into a suitable portfolio, though the final recommendation often still passes through a human adviser. For illiquid assets, AI helps estimate values when market prices are stale or missing, using comparable sales, cash flows and statistical models. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which gives a concrete universe for testing some of these portfolio methods.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Mean-variance optimisation is mature and widely implemented, and many portfolio systems now add constraints, transaction costs and factor exposures without much trouble. What remains hard is the tail: extreme losses, correlation breakdowns and regime changes are rare in historical data, so models often underestimate them. Sustainability factors are also unsettled, because definitions vary, data is patchy and the link between a score and financial risk is not stable. Pricing illiquid assets is another open problem, since private market valuations rely on models and appraisals rather than continuous trading. Personalised advice at scale faces limits in data privacy, suitability rules and the difficulty of modelling human goals that change over time. The honest limit is that AI can improve parts of portfolio construction, but it cannot remove uncertainty, and backtests can mislead when markets shift.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to see how individual goals, taxes and behavioural biases enter the process should turn to Personalised Wealth Advice. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance explains how objectives such as skewness, drawdown control and robust allocation are formulated and solved. Tail Risk Hedging covers the instruments and strategies used to protect against extreme market moves, including options, dynamic hedging and stress testing. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios examines how environmental, social and governance data is measured, integrated and challenged in allocation decisions. Pricing Illiquid Assets deals with private equity, real estate and other assets where no continuous market price exists, and where valuation models carry real model risk. Together these pages move from the individual investor to the mathematical core, then to the edges of risk, sustainability and illiquidity, which is where much of the unresolved work sits.
